name: Lettuce Earth fresh yield · per-area light-limited model (v3)
task: Earth fresh shoot mass per plant, mediated by fresh yield per square metre
sourceCitation: Carotti L, Graamans L, Puksic F, Butturini M, Meinen E, Heuvelink E, Stanghellini C (2021) Plant Factories Are Heating Up. Front. Plant Sci. 11:592171, doi:10.3389/fpls.2020.592171
method: Boosted regression trees on log(fresh yield per m2). Light enters as daily light integral; per-plant mass is served as per-area yield divided by the plant density the caller states.

dailyLightIntegral.note: PAR photons only; no conversion from global radiation is applied.

unit: g fresh shoot mass per plant

modelSelection.protocol: leave-one-experiment-out (GroupKFold, 4 folds, identical folds for every learner)
modelSelection.criterion: lowest out-of-fold MAE in g fresh mass per m2

lightDriverComparison.why: Every representation scored the same internal MAE, so internal validation could not separate them. The choice was made on agronomic grounds - daily light integral is the standard driver and the only one that makes studies with different photoperiods comparable - and every variant's result on the development set is reported here rather than suppressed.
lightDriverComparison.disclosure: Because the development-set numbers informed this choice, the development set is NOT counted as independent validation. The independent check is the Touliatos holdout below.

metricUnits: g fresh mass per m2, over the whole growth curve (not harvest-only)
inverseOfLogTransform: exp(); predictions are median-like, not mean-like

interval.kind: conformal residual quantiles on the log target (5% / 95%)
interval.coverageNote: Measured on the same out-of-fold predictions the quantiles come from, so it is descriptive, not independent evidence.

densityDomain.basis: Spans the studies examined: 25 (plant factory), 48 (greenhouse), 50 (horizontal hydroponic). Above ~200 plants/m2 the per-area identity is known to break - Touliatos measured 95 kg/m2 per occupied floor area at 1000 plants/m2, a figure that includes stacking.
densityDomain.warningOutside: per-plant mass outside this range extrapolates the identity itself

independent.study: Touliatos D, Dodd IC, McAinsh M (2016) Vertical farming increases lettuce yield per unit area compared to conventional horizontal hydroponics. Food and Energy Security 5(3):184-191, doi:10.1002/fes3.83

refused.why: The per-area identity assumes per-area yield does not depend on density. At 1000 plants/m2 Touliatos report 95 kg/m2 per occupied floor area, which includes stacking across layers, so the identity is known to break here. Refused rather than scored.

independent.verdict: Fails the 30% criterion; the improvement over v2 is real but the model is not validated for harvest forecasting.

development.note: Reported for transparency and for comparison with v2 on the same six observations. Not evidence of independent accuracy.

limitations: Fresh yield per square metre is higher in the training system (non-limiting CO2, optimal temperature, plant factory) than in an ambient-CO2 greenhouse, so an upward bias remains.
Density enters only through the per-area identity; the model does not learn how density changes per-area yield, and refuses above ~200 plants/m2 for that reason.
Cultivar is not a feature. Batavia Othilie (training) differs from Baby Cos and Green Oak (development) by 63% in the external study, which no recalibration can represent.
The light response is monotonic; the development data are not.
Root-zone temperature is required by the model and is not reported by either external study, so it is assumed equal to air temperature in both checks.
Earth only, within the declared domains, and not validated for harvest forecasting.

targetTransform.name: log
targetTransform.why: Fresh yield is strictly positive and varies over two orders of magnitude across the growth curve; the log target makes the error multiplicative and lets the conformal interval become a ratio. Predictions are therefore median-like, not mean-like.

servesAlongside: lettuce-earth-growth-v2 (byte-identical, still callable, still serving its 232 % external failure as the record that motivated v3)

workflow.note: The workflow passes the model's four recorded features, so it returns areal yield. Per-plant mass is areal yield divided by plantDensityPerM2; use POST /api/predict/lettuce-earth-growth-v3 to supply the density and the photoperiod that defines the daily light integral.

sourceType: external scientific data (not NASA): 4TU.ResearchData experiment tables
license: CC BY 4.0, declared in the dataset's RO-Crate (data/metadata/wur_lettuce_rocrate.json)
servedScope: Fresh yield per square metre inside the measured WUR domain, divided by the planting density the caller states. The pre-registered criterion was 30 % MAPE on an independent holdout; the model returned 41.6 % on Touliatos et al. 2016 data, so it is served as a research surface that reports its own failure, not as a forecast.

archivalRecord.served: research surface with the missed criterion stated
archivalRecord.reason: The pre-registered failure is published with the model; withdrawing it would also withdraw the evidence.

note: No operational forecast. This card describes what the model reproduces inside the measured domain; it is not a prediction of a future or unmeasured crop.
